authority: Current requirement-to-operation audit. Historical acceptance, source presence, route-name parity, fixtures, and certification receipts are not current functional completion evidence.

requirements.requirement: Audit and trace everything, log every issue before repair, and preserve continuity across reports and chat history.
requirements.evidence: This ledger now preserves the full requirement crosswalk and dependency order, but per-requirement source, owner, live-state, and contrary-evidence fields still need to be normalized before PX-OS-049 can close.

requirements.requirement: Diagnose long Codex startup rather than only PX extension activation.
requirements.evidence: PX registration timing was substituted for end-to-end Codex readiness; current logs/processes expose separate extension, Copilot, Python, MCP, and code-mode-host delays.

requirements.requirement: PX defines governance while Codex retains native host execution and approval authority.
requirements.evidence: The source labels Codex as executor owner, but Continue with Codex only prepares a JSON document and PX policy is not an enforceable Codex-host authority layer.

requirements.requirement: Resolve operation/permission conflicts between Codex and PX.
requirements.evidence: Codex approvals, repository instructions, PX claims/grants, and extension-owned executors remain distinct planes; the strictest-denial guidance exists but seamless enforcement does not.

requirements.requirement: Use 10-20 lightweight .agents facade skills and lazy-load one PX-native skill body after semantic or exact selection.
requirements.evidence: There are 16 facades, a maximum-three query and exact-one hydration broker, and 177 native packages; the Codex host still enumerates global skills directly.

requirements.requirement: Every PX skill has SKILL.md, capability.json, skill.yaml, contracts, tests, and resources.
requirements.evidence: All 177 current .px/skills directories contain all six required entries; operational creation, admission, comparison, rollback, and index consistency remain open.

requirements.requirement: Separate PX-standard, Microsoft/vendor, enterprise-restricted, and user-preserved skills without bleed.
requirements.evidence: PX index domains and UI tabs are separate; direct Codex global skill discovery bypasses that broker policy.

requirements.requirement: Preserve original user skills permanently, adapt into new candidates, and support comparison/selection/restore without destructive loss.
requirements.evidence: Two workspace copies and a user-original backup exist with 1,888 files, but comparison/adaptation/rollback is not a complete workflow and first initialization is not transactional.

requirements.requirement: Fix the pyproject.toml duplicate key error.
requirements.evidence: Python tomllib parses pyproject.toml successfully at version 0.7.0.dev0; generated packaging now rejects duplicate destinations. Skill-index projection drift remains separate.

requirements.requirement: Make the extension command and sidebar provider load correctly.
requirements.evidence: The current manifest contributes a webview and the commands; the long-lived VS Code main process predates the newest installation, so exact live behavior is not yet walked.

requirements.requirement: Populate the side panel with current truthful actions and data, including invalid-union diagnostics.
requirements.evidence: Inbound, operation, and outbound errors are separated in source, but subtask routing remains wrong and route parity does not prove downstream behavior.

requirements.requirement: Make the dashboard dense, responsive, unclipped, and free of wasted visual space.
requirements.evidence: Conflicting CSS ownership, fixed empty panels, clipped lifecycle content, and legacy overrides remain.

requirements.requirement: Provide a full Obsidian/GitNexus-quality Knowledge Graph rather than a generic sparse cluster view.
requirements.evidence: Overview clusters replace records, record views are capped, and fixed orbit/lane card layouts do not provide a progressive full map.

requirements.requirement: Connect experience, evidence, patterns, hypotheses, validation, learning, measured reuse, promotion, decay, hashes, A/B trials, and research validation.
requirements.evidence: Side-effect-free primitives and one cleanup build script exist; production controllers, CLI lifecycle, execution routing, UI, and general cross-run correlation are absent.

requirements.requirement: Implement the execution-placement add-on completely and connect GPU/CPU/parallel decisions to evidence.
requirements.evidence: Keep-current scoring and some hash gates exist, but the live scheduler/UI/benchmark/rollback lifecycle and Tier 4/5 outputs do not. No compatible CUDA executor is currently admitted, so CPU fallback is the only truthful route.

requirements.requirement: Complete the bounded-work architecture and update only changed pieces after first initialization.
requirements.evidence: Selected extension calls use bounded pools, but no unified cross-runtime Event Hub, dependency graph, State Bus, telemetry sampler, causal invalidation, or proven stable-idle behavior exists.

requirements.requirement: Chunk tests into affected sections, run safe groups in parallel, rerun only failures, and reserve whole testing for final certification.
requirements.evidence: Section/group/run-stale and bounded workers exist; eight required receipts are stale or failed and unchanged/incremental behavior is not currently proven.

requirements.requirement: Build a real visual Agent Builder using the supplied reference as a capability benchmark.
requirements.evidence: Current Agent Studio is a long form with scroll buttons; its schema lacks model/provider, memory/retrieval, structured I/O, variables, handoffs, preview, templates, and trace inspection.

requirements.requirement: Make agent execution real and truthful.
requirements.evidence: harness:px explicitly records model_invoked=false and supports only bounded local utility operations.

requirements.requirement: Make Workflow Studio a real visual, parallel, typed, traceable execution system.
requirements.evidence: The editor lacks mature canvas navigation and run overlays, runtime node kinds/config are cosmetic, and independent DAG branches execute serially.

requirements.requirement: Make canonical memory attach, lease, retrieval, and remediation actually work.
requirements.evidence: No pacifyX.workspaceRoot is configured and no active canonical memory lease/retrieval root is attached.

requirements.requirement: Make Projects, Plugins, Activity, Diagnostics, Runtime Core, Settings, and governed maintenance operational rather than informational.
requirements.evidence: These surfaces remain incomplete managers or status views and omit core lifecycle, cause, repair, placement, and configuration operations.

requirements.requirement: Integrate with Codex and Copilot seamlessly without stealing host authority.
requirements.evidence: PX registers a local model provider and MCP definition but has no chat participant or end-to-end session correlation; handoff is a JSON document.

requirements.requirement: Follow cleanup/storage rules and avoid filling the disk while preserving evidence and originals.
requirements.evidence: C: currently has about 334 GiB free, but current project-map history, operation-bus volume, installed generations, and dirty-tree growth are not governed by a current incremental retention proof.

requirements.requirement: Do not certify until the product is operational; distinguish operational health from evidence freshness and certification.
requirements.evidence: Completion schema 1.3 separates historical cards, current operational readiness, live verification, evidence freshness, and certification. Dashboard source now separates exact-host connectivity, per-feature availability, diagnostic validation, and certification; current-host behavior remains pending live walk.

requirements.requirement: Make every visible UI element perform a useful real operation with truthful success and failure acknowledgement.
requirements.evidence: Static action/handler parity is complete, but numerous controls only change local UI, open prose, or route to narrower backend semantics than their labels claim.
